text:
GruntWorx should inherit Instead’s reliability patterns, while defining its own API limits and vendor mappings. The main lessons are:

1. **Budget requests at every scope the vendor enforces.** Instead throttles per connection and API group, plus an app-wide ceiling. Defaults are **5 docs requests/minute per connection**, 50 for entities, and 500 app-wide; these are configuration defaults, not GruntWorx requirements. Unknown groups fall into a budgeted `default` bucket. Group checks precede the app check so rejected jobs do not consume app capacity. Respect `Retry-After` as seconds or an HTTP date. The normal retry bound is **10 retries**, roughly 4½ hours, but throttle rescheduling resets the counter—there is **no strict wall-clock deadline**. GruntWorx should subclass the neutral worker and supply its own throttle policy. [Throttle configuration](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/config/initializers/sidekiq.rb:101), [retry behavior](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/operation_worker.rb:9).

2. **Treat webhooks as an optimization backed by reconciliation.** Instead selects uploaded documents still `sent` after **1 hour**, or `processing` after **12 hours**, and stops selecting them after **2 days**; older records remain unchanged. It lists documents by entity/year with pagination, then individually fetches candidates missing from the listing. An individual document’s 404 means archived; a missing/inaccessible folder is skipped. Reconciliation operations make one attempt (`retry: 0`), leaving another sweep to retry. Both webhook and polling results use the same status mapper, preventing divergent behavior. GruntWorx needs equivalent recovery with explicitly chosen windows and deletion semantics. [Candidate windows](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/queries/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/reconcile_candidates_query.rb:8), [page reconciliation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/reconcile_statuses.rb:29), [individual fallback](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/reconcile_status.rb:38).

3. **Keep a shared failure vocabulary and separate upload from processing.** The common reasons are `unexpected`, `no_active_connection`, `network_error`, `unauthorized`, `api_error`, `exceeded`, `forbidden`, and `encrypted`. Instead maps `password_required` to `encrypted`; an unknown processing refusal becomes `error` without inventing a reason. Terminal upload refusals end the send; transient errors enter retries. Duplicate status reports are harmless, backward transitions are refused, and recovery from `error` to `processed` passes through `processing`. Successful recovery clears obsolete reasons. GruntWorx should translate its vocabulary at the adapter boundary. [Shared model](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:13), [refusal classification](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/refusals_helper.rb:8), [Instead status mapping](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/apply_processing_status.rb:10).

4. **Make signed-upload cassettes safe and reproducible.** Recording scrubs signed policy, credential and signature fields, plus OAuth secrets; Instead traffic also has bearer headers and tokens scrubbed. Tagged replay freezes time at the cassette’s earliest recording timestamp, so an old `ExpiresAt` remains meaningful; new recordings use real time. GruntWorx must extend vendor-specific scrubbing to its host and actual credential representation—the current token scrub is explicitly Instead-specific. Preserve production expiry checks rather than weakening them for fixtures. [Recording sanitization](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/spec/spec_helper.rb:164), [replay clock](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/spec/support/vcr_fixed_time.rb:3).

5. **Match entities conservatively and reuse durable links.** Existing links are found locally by firm, account/contact and entity type, across tax years, without spending an API request. Name matching considers only active, unlinked entities in the same firm/type and links **exactly one** candidate. It normalizes punctuation, Unicode whitespace and case; business names additionally normalize legal-form spellings and `&`/`and`. Personal matching permits account-name fallback only for a sole contact, then tries swapped first/last names if direct matching found nothing. Ambiguity produces no link and has a distinct metric outcome. GruntWorx should retain these safeguards while validating its own entity/type model. [Existing links](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/clients/find_entity.rb:24), [name matching](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/clients/link_entity_by_name.rb:47).

These conclusions come from the existing code; GruntWorx’s actual limits and API semantics still need validation. No files were changed.
